overview.text: An unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), often called a drone, is an aircraft with no pilot aboard. It may be controlled remotely by a person on the ground or fly autonomously; “unmanned” does not mean that people are uninvolved. The Federal Aviation Administration distinguishes the aircraft from an unmanned aircraft system (UAS), which includes the equipment needed to operate it. UAVs are useful for scientific observation and other work in remote or hazardous places, where flying without an onboard pilot can reduce risks to people. Their tasks include observing Earth, surveying land and crops, supporting firefighting, and military reconnaissance. Designs range from radio-controlled models to aircraft built for long-duration research flights.

key_facts.text: A UAV has no onboard pilot; it can be remotely controlled or autonomous.
A UAS includes the unmanned aircraft and the equipment needed to operate it.
People may still operate, monitor, or support a UAV from the ground.
NASA examples include using unmanned aircraft for Earth observation, wildfire support, and surveying land or crops.
Unmanned aircraft have been used for research in hazardous flight conditions and for military reconnaissance.
